# STIG finding map

Every finding in the **Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 Security Technical Implementation Guide** (Version 1, Release: 2 Benchmark Date: 01 Jul 2026), how this repo meets it, and what the scans found. SCAP content: scap-security-guide 0.1.82 (almalinux10).

How to read it: [README.md](README.md#reading-the-finding-map). Each finding's full DISA text is in the checklists under [checklists/](checklists/), which open in DISA STIG Viewer 3.

Targets: **Server image, not hardened**: the plain bootc server image, before the STIG layer (the starting point); **Server image, hardened**: the server-stig image, scanned in the registry before any host runs it; **bootc server (srv01)**: a running server installed over PXE from the server-stig image; **Workstation image, hardened**: the workstation-stig image, scanned in the registry; **bootc workstation (ws01)**: a running GNOME workstation installed over PXE from the workstation-stig image; **Traditional RPM server (rpm01)**: the comparison host, installed the way RHEL 8 is today (RPM Kickstart, then the Ansible Lockdown STIG role)

In the tables below, a host cell shows **OpenSCAP / Lockdown audit** where both scanners ran.

## Dispositions

- **Image build (OpenSCAP)**: Applied automatically when the image is built, by OpenSCAP's image-mode tool (oscap-im) running Red Hat's STIG content.
- **Image file**: A configuration file we ship in the image (named in 'Where').
- **Installer (Kickstart)**: Set when the host is installed, by the PXE Kickstart template.
- **VM disk template**: Set when the VM disk is built (bootc-image-builder config).
- **Site setting**: Needs a value only the site can give (servers, names, keys). The repo shows where it goes.
- **Exception**: Not met as written. The justification and approval status are recorded here.
- **Not applicable**: Does not apply to this system type, with the reason recorded.
- **Manual / procedural**: A person or a process checks this. Any automated result is shown for reference only.

| RHEL-10-000500 | V-281009 | Enable FIPS mode | Image file — FIPS mode is a kernel argument shipped in the image (bootc applies it on install and on every upgrade). OpenSCAP sets the FIPS crypto policy in the same build. The PXE installer also boots with fips=1 so keys made at install time are FIPS-generated. In the lab (AlmaLinux) the crypto modules are not FIPS-validated; on RHEL they are. | [01-fips.toml](../../images/stig/rootfs/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/01-fips.toml), [_kernel.j2](../../ansible/roles/bootc_pxe/templates/_kernel.j2) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅/✅ | ❌ | ✅/✅ | ✅/✅ |
